author: E. H. Fugate
title: Diocese of Gaylord announces clergy and diaconal appointments effective in 2026
text:
Bishop Jeffrey J. Walsh of the Diocese of Gaylord announced on April 22 a series of clergy and diaconal appointments, with most changes taking effect July 1, 2026.
These assignments affect leadership roles within the diocese as well as parish and deacon positions across the region. The changes are intended to support the ongoing pastoral needs of local Catholic communities.
Among the leadership changes, Reverend James P. Hayden will retire from his role as Vicar General and Moderator of the Curia. Reverend Charles G. Donajkowski will become Vicar General, moving from his current position as Pastor at St. Casimir Parish in Posen and St. Dominic Parish in Metz, where he also serves as Regional Vicar for the East Region. Reverend Matthew A. Furgiuele is appointed Judicial Vicar while continuing his service at St. Joseph Parish in East Jordan.
Additional appointments include Reverend Michael D. Class, SJ becoming Spiritual Director for Permanent Diaconate Formation Program and Administrator for several parishes; Reverend T. Patrick Maher transitioning to Co-coordinator for Native American Ministry; and Deacon Curtis P. Chambers also taking up a co-coordinator role while maintaining his existing ministries.
Parish assignments see several priests moving or adding responsibilities among parishes throughout the diocese, such as Reverend James M. Bearss serving both Divine Mercy Parish in Manistee and St. Joseph Parish in Onekama, and Reverend Donald L. Libby transferring to Cross in the Woods Parish along with other new pastoral duties.
Diaconal assignments effective April 18, 2026 include Deacons Jason P. Maday, Kenneth J. Plude, Steven H. Sandoval Jr., Neil E. Witkowski, and Brian M Wojtkowiak receiving new placements at various parishes across northern Michigan.
The Diocese of Gaylord is home to roughly 45,000 Catholics served by its network of 75 parishes and 21 Catholic schools; it also supports a Catholic hospital along with multiple day care centers and special social service facilities according to diocesan statistics.
These transitions reflect ongoing efforts by diocesan leadership to meet spiritual needs throughout their communities.
